harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a systemd-managed Python inventory app on node1 serving JSON inventory data over TCP port 8181, opened the firewalld port, and confirmed the service works with SELinux in Enforcing mode (process runs as unconfined_service_t, no AVC denials). Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured a pre-restart baseline (boot ID, service/port/HTTP state), triggered systemctl reboot, confirmed the connection dropped then recovered, verified the boot ID changed, and re-verified SELinux Enforcing, service active, port listening, no AVC denials, and correct inventory data served post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: confirmed RHEL 10, SELinux Enforcing (targeted policy), no pre-existing inventory app, firewalld active with no ports open, port 8181 pre-labeled intermapper_port_t in SELinux port policy
Created /opt/inventory/inventory.json (sample stock data) and /opt/inventory/app.py (Python ThreadingHTTPServer serving JSON on 0.0.0.0:8181)
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory-app.service so the app starts on boot and restarts on failure
Opened firewalld port 8181/tcp permanently and reloaded

Verified the service listens on 8181, runs under SELinux context system_u:system_r:unconfined_service_t:s0, produces no AVC denials, and that curl to $NODE_IP:8181/inventory returns HTTP 200 with correct JSON while getenforce reports Enforcing
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, SELinux mode, service status, port listener state, HTTP check
Triggered systemctl reboot on node1 in the background so the acknowledgement returned before the node disconnected

Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed (f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c -> d8f33669-0828-4748-9d64-c51d027f1d9f) and uptime -s advanced, proving an actual OS restart occurred (not just a service restart)

Post-restart verification: SELinux still Enforcing, inventory-app.service active (auto-started via systemd enable), port 8181 listening, process still unconfined_service_t, no AVC denials, firewalld still lists 8181/tcp, curl returns HTTP 200 with intact inventory JSON

evidence.requirement: Inventory app serves over TCP port 8181
evidence.summary: systemd unit started and enabled; ss shows LISTEN on 0.0.0.0:8181; curl to $NODE_IP:8181/inventory returns HTTP 200 with the inventory JSON body

evidence.requirement: SELinux mandatory access control remains in enforcing mode while the app serves traffic
evidence.summary: getenforce reports Enforcing at the same time curl succeeds; process context confirmed system_u:system_r:unconfined_service_t:s0 with no AVC denials via ausearch
Captured boot_id, uptime -s, SELinux Enforcing, service active/enabled, port listening, and HTTP 200 response before reboot
systemctl reboot launched in background with disown; exec call returned 'reboot-triggered' successfully before the node went unreachable
Two consecutive polls timed out (node down mid-reboot), then exec succeeded again with a new boot_id (d8f33669-...) and reset uptime -s, proving a genuine OS restart rather than a service bounce

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and SELinux enforcement
evidence.summary: After restart: getenforce Enforcing, inventory-app.service active, port 8181 listening, process context still unconfined_service_t, no AVC denials, firewalld still allows 8181/tcp, and curl returns HTTP 200 with the same intact inventory JSON data
